title: Securing Employees’ AI Use Requires a Unified Architecture
summary: Falcon Guardian brings together complementary security mechanisms to deliver visibility, protection, and response across AI interactions and agent activity.
body_markdown:
AI is changing how employees work. From browser-based AI applications and coding assistants to autonomous agents that access tools, data, and systems, AI is becoming an integral part of everyday workflows. Much of this activity happens on the endpoint, where AI interactions can translate into real system actions.


Securing employees’ use of AI requires more than visibility into which applications employees use or what they send to AI models. Security teams must also understand what agents are instructed to do, how they communicate, and what they execute. No single feature can do this alone. It’s only possible with multiple security capabilities working in concert across each organization’s AI estate.


CrowdStrike® Falcon Guardian™ brings together complementary security mechanisms to deliver visibility, protection, and response across AI interactions and agent activity. Here, we detail these capabilities and how they help security teams better understand AI activity and risk.


## Layered Security for AI on the Endpoint


AI activity spans multiple layers, from employee interactions with AI applications to agents communicating with models and executing actions on the endpoint. Securing this activity requires complementary visibility and security controls at each layer.


Securing a single layer is not sufficient to gain a full picture of all AI usage. A browser extension, for example, would only be able to look at traffic going to and from web-based agents and AI tools, completely missing activity agents executed on the endpoint. Similarly, agent hooks would miss AI web apps and any prompts transiting through there; it would not be able to discover agents on the endpoint. The CrowdStrike Falcon® sensor is capable of seeing AI traffic, supplies runtime visibility, and allows for agent discovery of even dormant agents; however, it does not directly hook into the agent’s inference framework.


It takes multiple layers to get the full picture and to have sufficient security and visibility to apply defense in depth.


Falcon Guardian extends security beyond individual AI interactions to the communications and underlying system activity that AI agents generate.


Figure 1. Falcon Guardian combines complementary security mechanisms across AI interactions, communications, and endpoint execution. CrowdStrike® Agent Graph connects this activity into a unified relational view, from prompt to impact.


## Enforce Security Policies Across AI Activity


Visibility is only the starting point. Falcon Guardian enables security teams to enforce policies across supported AI interactions and agent activity, with controls tailored to where AI operates.


For supported browser-based AI interactions, policies can report, block, or transform content to help govern AI use and protect sensitive information. Agent-level hooks extend policy enforcement into supported AI agents, enabling security teams to inspect interactions and block potentially dangerous actions before execution.


At the operating system level, the Falcon sensor provides independent runtime protection, detecting and blocking supported malicious behavior even when an agent's initial action was permitted.


Together, these complementary controls help organizations govern AI use and protect against threats across the interaction and execution layers.


## Understand Agent Behavior from Prompt to Impact


When an AI agent takes action, individual prompts, tool calls, and endpoint events tell only part of the story. A process accessing a sensitive file may appear routine on its own, but the instructions and agent activity that led to it can reveal a security threat. Security teams need to connect these events to understand what happened, why it happened, and what was affected.


Falcon Guardian, powered by CrowdStrike Agent Graph, connects agents, sessions, models, tools, skills, MCP servers, processes, files, and related security events into a unified investigative context.


The Falcon Guardian session graph reveals the causal sequence within an individual agent session, tracing instructions and tool calls through downstream execution. The Footprint View extends this understanding across related agents, users, tools, and resources to help analysts assess the scope and potential blast radius of a threat. Instead of investigating disconnected signals, security teams can trace suspicious agent behavior to its origin, understand its consequences, and determine where to respond.


## Discover AI Activity and Detect Threats


Falcon Guardian brings AI security into the Falcon console to help security teams maintain visibility into AI adoption, monitor activity, and identify threats across their endpoints.


Agent Inventory reveals known and shadow AI agents, including active and dormant installations. Prompt Activity provides visibility into supported AI interactions, including the applications and models employees use. Detections bring together AI-specific threats, such as prompt injection and malicious skills, with suspicious agent behavior and Falcon endpoint detections. This helps security teams identify threats both within AI interactions and when agent activity translates into malicious system execution.


Together, these capabilities help security teams move beyond isolated AI activity logs to discover unmanaged AI, identify emerging risks, and prioritize threats that require attention.


## One Architecture for Securing AI on the Endpoint


By connecting AI interactions, communications, and endpoint execution, Falcon Guardian gives security teams a more complete understanding of how AI operates and where risks emerge. With unified visibility, protection, and response across supported AI activity, organizations can govern employee use of AI, investigate threats from prompt to impact, and accelerate AI adoption with confidence.
